note: What's new, newest first. Every change a viewer can notice adds a line to the top release in the same commit. Rules: CHANGELOG-RULES.md. Checked by scripts/check-changelog.mjs (pnpm check).

releases.title: A start page and intros on Roku
highlights: Roku opens on a start page with a big featured title, Continue watching, your apps and free live TV.

changes.text: A soft fade under the phone's status bar keeps the time and battery readable over scrolling posters.
Home on Android has The Hunger Games section in its colours, with a switch between story and release order.
Live TV on Android lists all the free channels Windows has, grouped by country, before your own.
Pulling past the top or bottom of a page on Android is smooth again, even straight after opening the app.
Tapping the video on Android no longer jumps playback; only the timeline moves it.
Android looks as it did on 18 November again; sign-in, sync, invite codes, sleep timer and Stats still work.
Roku opens on a start page: a greeting, a featured title, Continue watching, Apps and free live TV.
Hunger Games and Marvel films play their short intro on Roku too. Any button skips it.

releases.title: Glass navigation and clearer updates
highlights: TVM now distinguishes a failed update check from a current build.
The navigation bar has clearer glass, and phone layout keeps the artwork and controls readable.

changes.text: Update now waits for the new engine before saying TVM has restarted.
Failed update checks show the error instead of suggesting the app is up to date.
Windows retries sooner when it cannot check or download an update.
The app-wide Back button is gone. Settings and the TV guide have their own header arrows.
The mouse pointer stays visible in the Windows TV guide.
The navigation pill shows more of the artwork through Liquid Glass.
Keyboard and remote focus use a neutral highlight without a blue outline.
Portrait phones keep the full Hub artwork and give the welcome text its own space.

releases.title: Windows parity, Hub, Bloom ribbons and glass
highlights: Windows gets the Hub page, wide Movie and Series lanes, and Hunger Games and Doomsday intros.
Liquid Glass refracts more clearly over new blue-violet Bloom silk ribbons on Windows and web.
Windows Settings gains Update now, Settings About trailer playback and Developer tools.
All platforms share the corrected version badge without the placeholder tag.

changes.text: The navigation bar is clear Liquid Glass again instead of a flat grey bar, and stays at the top on Live TV.
The Hunger Games row runs once in story order, from The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes to Mockingjay Part 2.
Hovered posters no longer cover the row heading or get their tops cut off.
Row arrows come back when you return to a row, and the hero fades into the rows below without a hard line.
The glow under Play and Watch the saga fades out softly instead of ending in a square edge.
The blue ribbon background now plays only on the Hub and profile chooser, and no longer cuts off.
The back button is a plain, thicker arrow without the circle behind it.
Player buttons show the same glass as the details buttons when you hover them, and nothing when you don't.
The mouse pointer comes back in the TV guide as soon as you move it.
Added the Hub start page with greeting, hero spotlight, Continue watching, apps and free live channels.
Movies and Series now show hero backdrops, 16:9 widescreen cards and genre-filtered carousels.
Hunger Games and Avengers Doomsday intros play once per session over stream loading and skip on any key.
Tuned PyGlass bevel refraction, chromatic rim edges and Bloom ribbons over translucent Settings cards.
Settings About reads the real build version and Update now checks and applies updates on demand.
Settings About opens the TVM trailer and Developer gains diagnostics, cache clear and intro replays.

highlights: A new Home: no more glass box over the spotlight, a centred menu bar and a cleaner font.
Films and shows now start in their original language at the best real resolution, often 4K.
Click the picture to pause, double-click for fullscreen, and the controls show in fullscreen.
This is a test build. Read Known issues below before you report a bug.

changes.text: The spotlight drops the glass box: the title sits on the art with a soft fade behind it.
The menu bar is centred and solid, and Search is now a magnifier button at its end.
Looping rows light up only the card you are on, and a hovered card is no longer cut off.
TVM now uses the Geist font, and buttons are rounded rectangles instead of pills.
TVM picks the original-language audio and the highest real resolution, and skips upscaled copies.
Click the picture to pause or play, and double-click to go fullscreen.
The player controls now appear in fullscreen when you move the mouse.
A TV-style guide shows what is on now and next, with a red line for the current time.
A key set for your account shows up within a minute, without restarting TVM.
Patch notes like these open as a pop-up after an update. Close it with Got it.
Verification and password reset emails are live for new accounts.

highlights: Profile pictures now show the characters from each show and film, not the actors.
A Real-Debrid key set for your account now works within seconds.

changes.text: Every avatar set now uses pictures of the characters, cropped to their faces.
A key the owner sets for your account no longer takes up to 10 minutes to start working.

releases.title: Sign-in fix for Windows
highlights: On Windows, signing in works straight after TVM updates itself.

changes.text: After TVM updates on Windows, it updates its engine too, so sign-in and new features work at once.

releases.title: Simpler sign-in, account and plans
highlights: Signing in is one step at a time: email, then password, with one clear button.
On Roku, scan a QR code with your phone to sign in. No typing on the remote.
Waiting for approval now says so plainly and checks again by itself.
The account and plans pages are tidier, with one recommended plan.

changes.text: Email first, then password, with a show-password button and clear messages when something is wrong.
Create account is a link under the sign-in box instead of a row of tabs.
Roku shows a QR code and a short code. Approve it on your phone and the TV signs itself in.
"Waiting for approval" replaces codes like awaiting_activation, and it rechecks every minute.
Account is a short list: plan, Real-Debrid, Live TV and status, with Sign out at the bottom.
Two plan cards side by side, the popular one marked, one button each.

releases.title: Skip intros, subtitles, and private accounts
highlights: Skip intros, recaps and credits, with an Up next countdown when the credits roll.
Subtitles in your languages, trailers, film collections and new-episode dates.
Accounts now live on TVM's own private server. Members need to sign up again.
Your stats: hours watched, streak and top genres, with history you can clear.

changes.text: Skip intro, recap and credits. Choose Off, a Skip button, or skip automatically in Settings.
Up next counts down to the next episode when the credits start. Autoplay can be turned off.
Subtitles from OpenSubtitles in your preferred languages, remembered per profile.
Trailers, the rest of a film collection in order, and the date of a show's next episode.
Anime shows its English title when there is one.
A New episodes this week row for shows you are watching or saved.
Optional muted trailer previews on the big title at the top, on computers.
Your stats: hours watched, finished titles, streak and top genres. Clear history any time.
Sign-ins and Real-Debrid tokens moved to TVM's private accounts server, encrypted there.
Members need to sign up again once. The owner switches each account on.
Developer codes are gone. The owner manages accounts from a private web dashboard.

releases.title: Glass, longer rows, and your other services
highlights: Rows keep going: far more films and shows per category, loading as you scroll.
Sign in to Netflix, Disney+ and others, then open titles there from TVM.
Kids profiles, age limits, PIN locks and character profile pictures.
Free live channels, including BBC One, BBC News and CBeebies (UK only).

changes.text: Glass redone to match iOS 27: clearer centre, sharper edges, brighter highlights.
Each category now holds dozens of titles and loops round without a visible seam.
Big releases get their own spot. Sunrise on the Reaping now, Avengers: Doomsday from 9 December.
IMDb rating on every title. Hover it for the top reviews, click it to open IMDb.
Sign in to your streaming services once and open shows in them from TVM.
Kids profiles, age limits from UK and US certificates (genre when there is none), and PIN locks.
Pick a profile picture from Hunger Games, Avengers, Jujutsu Kaisen and more.
A Free channels row that works without a login or playlist.
Volume slider now goes to 200%. It no longer drops back under 100%.
Starts at the best quality your screen can show, unless you pick one yourself.
New loading animation that speeds up as the stream comes in.
Typing no longer gets cut off when results arrive.
A Back button on most pages.
What's new shows once after an update, in the corner of Home. Every version's notes live in Settings.
Roku shows when an update is out, and TVM on your computer can install it for you.

releases.title: TVM everywhere
highlights: One app on Windows, Mac, Linux, iPhone, Android, Roku and the web.
Real-Debrid and your own Live TV playlist, set up from Account.
Liquid Glass across the app, with Clear and Frosted styles.

changes.text: A single TVM.exe that installs and updates itself.
Runs on its own, with no PC needed.
Categories loop, and keep their place when you come back.
A television-style search page.
New controls, a draggable volume bar and readable menus.
"Who's watching?" chooser with up to 10 profiles.
Sign in, create an account or use a developer code.
